about: The scripted AI lesson for p1-power (2026-11-17, Phase B, brief docs/briefs/2026-11-15-script-four-topics.md): every word she sees is written here once and checked (tools/check-script.js, tools/review-lesson.js --script). The AI only marks her typed answers (choosing a branch written here), answers her own questions, and sorts her messages. It opens with two recall questions from p1-energy-stores and p1-efficiency.

steps.text: Welcome! This lesson is about power: how fast energy is transferred, how to work it out, and the units it is measured in.

steps.question: First, two quick questions from earlier lessons. What unit is energy measured in?
steps.right: Yes: energy is measured in joules (J).

wrong.newton: Not quite: joules (J). Newtons are the unit of force.
wrong.metre: Not quite: joules (J). Metres measure distance.

idk.hint: The unit of energy is named after the scientist James Joule. Which button is it?

steps.question: Second: a motor is supplied with 400 J and transfers 100 J usefully. What is its efficiency, as a percentage?

wrong.decimal: Nearly: 0.25 is the decimal. As a percentage, multiply by 100: 25%.
wrong.upside: Not quite: 25%. Put the useful energy on top: 100 ÷ 400 = 0.25, which is 25%.

idk.hint: Divide the useful energy, 100, by the total, 400. Then multiply by 100.

steps.text: Now this lesson. Two kettles each heat the same water by the same amount. One takes 2 minutes and the other takes 4. Both transfer the same energy to the water, but the first does it twice as fast.
A rate is how much happens each second. Speed is a rate: the metres you travel each second.
The rate at which energy is transferred is called power: the energy transferred each second. The faster kettle has twice the power.
Power is measured in watts (W). 1 watt is 1 joule transferred every second.

steps.question: A lamp transfers 60 J every second. What is its power?
steps.right: Yes: 60 W. A watt is a joule each second, so 60 J every second is 60 W.

wrong.other: Not quite: 60 W. A watt is a joule each second.
wrong.unit: Nearly: the number is right, but power is in watts. 60 J every second is 60 W.
wrong.one: Not quite: 60 W. 1 W would be 1 J each second. 60 J each second is 60 W.

idk.hint: One watt is one joule every second. So how many watts is 60 joules every second?

steps.answerWhy: A watt is a joule each second, so 60 J every second is 60 W.

steps.text: The equation is P = E ÷ t: power = energy transferred ÷ time. P is the power in watts (W), E is the energy transferred in joules (J) and t is the time in seconds (s).

A more powerful machine does not always transfer more energy in total: it transfers energy faster. A crane that lifts a car in 5 s and one that takes 20 s transfer the same energy, but the faster crane has four times the power.

steps.question: Two motors lift the same load to the same height. Motor X takes 10 s and motor Y takes 20 s. Which is true?

options.text: X has twice the power of Y
X transfers more energy than Y
Y has more power, because it works for longer

steps.right: Yes: they transfer the same energy, but X does it in half the time, so X has twice the power.

wrong.other: Not quite. X has twice the power: the same energy in half the time.
wrong.energy: Not quite: same load, same height, so the same energy. X transfers it in half the time, so X has twice the power.
wrong.longer: Not quite: taking longer means a lower power. X transfers the same energy in half the time, so X has twice the power.

idk.hint: Both lift the same load the same height, so the energy is the same. Which one transfers it faster?

steps.answerWhy: The energy is the same, but X transfers it in half the time, so X has twice the power.

steps.prompt: In one line: what is power, and what unit is it measured in?
points: the energy transferred each second (the rate of energy transfer)
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: power is the energy transferred each second, measured in watts.

steps.text: Here is a worked example. Tap "Show the first step" under it to see each step in turn.
steps.question: A light bulb transfers 1800 J in 3 minutes. What is its power?
steps: Write the equation and put in the numbers: P = E ÷ t = 1800 ÷ 180.

steps.question: Your turn. A runner transfers 12 000 J in 60 s. What is the runner's power, in watts?

wrong.times: Not quite: 200 W. Divide the energy by the time, do not multiply: 12 000 ÷ 60 = 200 W.
wrong.upside: Not quite: 200 W. Put the energy on top: P = 12 000 ÷ 60 = 200 W.

idk.hint: Use P = E ÷ t: divide the energy, 12 000, by the time, 60.

steps.text: Big powers are often given in kilowatts (kW): 1 kW = 1000 W. A 2 kW heater has a power of 2000 W.
Power stations are measured in megawatts (MW): 1 MW = 1 000 000 W, a million watts. Change kilowatts and megawatts into watts before you calculate.
To find the energy, rearrange to E = P × t. To find the time, t = E ÷ P. If you are unsure, put the numbers into P = E ÷ t first, then rearrange.

steps.question: A 2 kW heater is on for 30 s. How much energy does it transfer, in joules?

wrong.nokw: Not quite: 60 000 J. Change kilowatts to watts first: 2 kW = 2000 W. Then E = 2000 × 30 = 60 000 J.
wrong.divide: Not quite: 60 000 J. To find the energy, multiply: E = P × t = 2000 × 30 = 60 000 J.

idk.hint: First, 2 kW in watts is 2000 W. Then multiply by the time, 30 s.

steps.question: How long does a 500 W microwave take to transfer 30 000 J, in seconds?

wrong.times: Not quite: 60 s. To find the time, divide the energy by the power: 30 000 ÷ 500 = 60 s.
wrong.upside: Not quite: 60 s. Put the energy on top: t = 30 000 ÷ 500 = 60 s.

idk.hint: Use t = E ÷ P: divide 30 000 by 500.

steps.question: A 1.5 kW kettle is on for 2 minutes. How much energy does it transfer, in joules?

wrong.none: Not quite: 180 000 J. Both need changing: 1.5 kW = 1500 W, and 2 minutes = 120 s. Then E = 1500 × 120 = 180 000 J.
wrong.nokw: Not quite: 180 000 J. The time is right in seconds, but the power must be in watts: 1.5 kW = 1500 W. E = 1500 × 120 = 180 000 J.
wrong.nomin: Not quite: 180 000 J. The power is right in watts, but the time must be in seconds: 2 minutes = 120 s. E = 1500 × 120 = 180 000 J.

idk.hint: Change both: 1.5 kW is 1500 W, and 2 minutes is 120 s. Then multiply them.

steps.prompt: In one line: what units must the power, energy and time be in before you use P = E ÷ t?
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: power in watts, energy in joules and time in seconds.

steps.text: Some real powers: a hairdryer is about 2000 W, a kettle 2000 to 3000 W, and an electric car's motor 100 to 300 kW.
A large power station gives out about 1 to 2 gigawatts (GW). A gigawatt is 1 000 000 000 W, a thousand million watts.

steps.question: Which of these transfers energy fastest?
steps.right: Yes: 2 GW is 2 000 000 000 W, far more than the others.

wrong.other: Not quite: the 2 GW power station. A gigawatt is a thousand million watts.
wrong.kettle: Not quite: 3 kW is only 3000 W. The power station, 2 GW, is 2 000 000 000 W.
wrong.car: Not quite: 300 kW is 300 000 W. The power station, 2 GW, is 2 000 000 000 W.

idk.hint: Giga is bigger than mega, and mega is bigger than kilo. Which button has giga?

steps.answerWhy: 2 GW is 2 000 000 000 W, far more than 3 kW or 300 kW.

steps.prompt: In one line: what does it mean that a kettle has a higher power than a phone charger?
points: the kettle transfers more energy each second
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: the kettle transfers more energy each second than the charger.

steps.text: When a force moves an object, it transfers energy. The energy transferred when a force moves something is called the work done.
The equation is W = F s: work done = force × distance. W is the work done in joules (J), F is the force in newtons (N) and s is the distance moved along the line of the force in metres (m).
One joule of work is done when a force of 1 newton moves something 1 metre. A newton-metre (N m) is therefore the same as a joule: 20 N m is 20 J.
Here is a worked example. Its steps open one at a time.
steps.question: A force of 3000 N pushes a car 20 m. How much work is done?
steps: Write the equation: W = F s.

steps.question: Your turn. A force of 50 N pushes a box 4 m along the floor. How much work is done, in joules?

wrong.other: Not quite: 200 J. W = F s = 50 × 4 = 200 J.
wrong.divide: Not quite: 200 J. Multiply the force by the distance: 50 × 4 = 200 J.
wrong.add: Not quite: 200 J. Multiply, do not add: 50 × 4 = 200 J.

idk.hint: Use W = F s: multiply the force, 50, by the distance, 4.

steps.text: Work done moves energy between stores. Lifting a box fills its gravitational potential store. Pushing a box against friction warms the box and the floor, so the energy goes to thermal stores.
Power is also the rate of doing work: P = W ÷ t. P is the power in watts (W), W is the work done in joules (J) and t is the time in seconds (s).

steps.question: A crane does 60 000 J of work lifting a load in 30 s. What is its power, in watts?

wrong.times: Not quite: 2000 W. Divide the work by the time: 60 000 ÷ 30 = 2000 W.

idk.hint: Use P = W ÷ t: divide 60 000 by 30.

steps.prompt: In one line: what is work done, and how is it linked to power?
points: the energy transferred when a force moves something (W = F s)
power is work done divided by time
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: work done is the energy transferred when a force moves something, W = F s, and power is the work done each second, P = W ÷ t.

steps.text: Now for a short quiz: six questions on the whole lesson. Take your time.

steps.question: Quiz, question 1 of 6: a motor transfers 500 J in 10 s. What is its power, in watts?

wrong.other: Not quite: 50 W. P = E ÷ t = 500 ÷ 10 = 50 W.

steps.question: Quiz, question 2 of 6: a heater has a power of 3 kW. What is that in watts?

wrong.other: Not quite: 3000 W. 1 kW = 1000 W, so 3 kW = 3000 W.

steps.question: Quiz, question 3 of 6: a 100 W lamp is on for 1 minute. How much energy does it transfer, in joules?
steps.right: Yes: 1 minute is 60 s, and E = P × t = 100 × 60 = 6000 J.

wrong.other: Not quite: 6000 J. 1 minute is 60 s, and E = P × t = 100 × 60 = 6000 J.

steps.answerWhy: 1 minute is 60 s, so E = P × t = 100 × 60 = 6000 J.

steps.question: Quiz, question 4 of 6: what unit is power measured in?
steps.right: Yes: watts. 1 W is 1 J each second.

wrong.other: Not quite: watts. 1 W is 1 J each second.

steps.answerWhy: Power is measured in watts: 1 W is 1 J each second.

steps.question: Quiz, question 5 of 6: a force of 20 N moves a box 5 m. How much work is done, in joules?

wrong.other: Not quite: 100 J. W = F s = 20 × 5 = 100 J.

steps.question: Quiz, question 6 of 6: a 3 kW kettle heats some water in 2 minutes. How long would a 1.5 kW kettle take to transfer the same energy?
steps.right: Yes: half the power, so twice the time for the same energy.

wrong.other: Not quite: 4 minutes. Half the power transfers the same energy in twice the time.

steps.answerWhy: Half the power transfers the same energy in twice the time: 4 minutes.
